items.t: Anti-Vascular Endothelial Growth Factor for Non-Proliferative Diabetic Retinopathy Without Center-Involving Diabetic Macular Edema: An Updated Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials
items.sum: We evaluated the functional and anatomical outcomes of anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (anti-VEGF) therapy in non-proliferative diabetic retinopathy (NPDR) without center-involving diabetic macular edema (CI-DME), following PRISMA 2020 guidelines (PROSPERO: CRD420261319796).  Four trials comprising 1,228 participants were included, evaluating aflibercept, ranibizumab delivered through the Port Delivery System, and tarcocimab tedromer.

items.t: Network Meta-Analysis of Complement Inhibitors for Geographic Atrophy in Age-Related Macular Degeneration
items.sum: Pegcetacoplan (PEG) and avacincaptad pegol (ACP) are approved complement inhibitors for geographic atrophy (GA) secondary to age-related macular degeneration, yet direct comparative evidence is lacking.  We conducted a PROSPERO-registered frequentist network meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials of complement inhibitors for GA.

items.t: Angiopoietin-2 in retinal vascular fibrosis: Mechanisms and therapeutic implications for diabetic retinopathy
items.sum: Retinal vascular fibrosis is a pathological hallmark of advanced diabetic retinopathy (DR), marking the transition from reversible vascular dysfunction to irreversible structural damage.  Emerging evidence has established angiopoietin-2 (Ang-2) as a crucial initiating factor in retinal vascular fibrosis.

items.t: Insights into the modulation of age-related macular degeneration: Molecular and systems-level perspectives
items.sum: In developed countries, age-related macular degeneration (AMD) is the leading cause of visual impairment in the aging population.  Understanding of its pathogenesis is limited and the number of patients is predicted to continue rising.
